records.title: Continental Tire Tread Separation Recall (21-inch All-Season)
records.description: Certain Equinox EVs fitted with 21-inch Continental CrossContact tires were built with a nonconforming tread-base rubber compound (inadequate sulfur level) from Continental DOT manufacturing week 4024 (week of Oct 6, 2024). The defective compound can allow partial or full tread detachment at speed, risking loss of control. This is NHTSA recall 25V704 (GM N252525030), covering roughly 22,900 vehicles (Equinox EV plus Cadillac Optiq); the 21-inch tires are standard on RS and optional on LT1/LT2.
records.solution: Under recall 25V704, dealers inspect all four tires and replace any tire manufactured during DOT week 4024 free of charge. Owners who already paid for replacement can apply to Continental for reimbursement. Check the DOT date code stamped on the tire sidewall.
symptoms: Vibration or thumping from a tire at speed
Visible tread lifting, bulging, or chunking on the tread/sidewall
Localized or unusual tread wear
Sudden tire failure or blowout
Loss of vehicle control from tread detachment

records.title: Front Footwell Water Leak (HVAC Drain / Body Seam Seal)
records.description: Owners of 2024-2025 Equinox EVs report water pooling in the front (often passenger) footwell, especially with A/C running while driving or after rain. GM traced it to the HVAC drain tube becoming disconnected from the bulkhead and to gaps in the body seam sealer under the carpet, and issued Service Update N252528650 / TSB 25-NA-149 directing dealers to water-test, reseal the body seam, and reconnect the drain. Standing water risks soaked carpet, odor/mold, and corrosion of underfloor electrical connectors.
records.solution: Per GM TSB 25-NA-149 / Service Update N252528650, technicians pull back the carpet, inspect and reseat the HVAC drain tube, confirm the leak with a water test, and seal the body seam with compound (no parts required). Dealers also remediate unsold lot inventory. Dry out carpet/padding to prevent mold.
symptoms: Water pooling in the front (often passenger) footwell
Wet or soaked carpet and floor padding
Leak appears mainly with A/C on while driving
Musty / mildew odor in the cabin
Damp underfloor wiring or connectors

records.title: High-Voltage Battery Fault / Sudden State-of-Charge Drop to 0% (Bricking)
records.description: Some Equinox EV owners have experienced high-voltage battery faults where the vehicle abruptly drops from a healthy state of charge to 0% and loses all drive power, requiring a tow, sometimes preceded by an in-app 'high-voltage battery' warning. A widely reported case (Tom Moloughney's ~9,500-mile Equinox EV dropping from 46% to 0%) is documented by InsideEVs. NHTSA characterizes this as a software error usually cleared by resetting codes; note it is a shared GM Ultium phenomenon (also Blazer EV, Cadillac Lyriq/Optiq/Vistiq) and is rare relative to fleet size, and is distinct from the separate 12V auxiliary-battery bricking issue.
records.solution: Treat any sudden drop to 0% or a high-voltage warning as a fault: stop, use roadside assistance, and have the vehicle towed to a GM EV-certified dealer to pull BMS logs. Reported fixes to date involve clearing error codes / software updates (and in some cases correcting a corroded battery-cable pin or a failing 12V battery) under warranty; keep the vehicle on the latest BMS/control software.
symptoms: App or cluster high-voltage battery fault warning
State of charge dropping suddenly from a normal level to 0%
Complete loss of drive power requiring a tow
'Service High Voltage System' message
Vehicle temporarily unresponsive / non-recognition of charger

records.title: LED Headlamp Snow and Slush Buildup (Winter Visibility)
records.description: In snow and slush, the Equinox EV's deeply recessed LED headlamps progressively pack with snow/ice and dim or black out, because the LEDs produce almost no waste heat to melt accumulation (unlike halogen units) and the deep-set lens design traps buildup. Owners across the Equinox EV forum and complaint sites report having to stop and manually clear the lamps during winter driving, a genuine nighttime visibility/safety concern.
records.solution: No factory fix or recall; mitigation is owner-side. Periodically stop and manually clear snow/slush from the headlamp recesses, apply a hydrophobic coating, or fit aftermarket lens protection. There is no headlight washer/heater on these units, so proactive clearing in heavy snow is required.
symptoms: Headlights dim or go dark in snow/slush
Visible snow or ice packed into the headlamp recess
Reduced forward visibility at night in winter
Need to stop and manually clear the lamps repeatedly

records.title: Loss of Propulsion / Vehicle Control Software Defect (Power-Loss Recall)
records.description: A vehicle-control software defect can cause the 2025 Equinox EV to unexpectedly lose propulsion or fail to operate as intended while driving, with owners reporting sudden power drops, hesitation, stalling, or propulsion/stability warnings. GM issued an early-2026 recall of roughly 100,000+ Equinox EVs (2025-2026 model years) to correct propulsion-control logic; the root cause is software calibration in the vehicle's control modules, not hardware failure.
records.solution: Dealer software/calibration update to the affected vehicle-control modules at no cost under the recall. Owners should run their VIN through the NHTSA or Chevrolet recall lookup; if any propulsion or stability warning appears while driving, stop and schedule service immediately.
symptoms: Sudden, unexpected loss of motive power while driving
Reduced power / failure to accelerate (limp behavior)
Propulsion or stability warning messages on the cluster
Hesitation or stalling
Vehicle disabling itself requiring a tow

records.title: Slow DC Fast Charging and Early Thermal Derating
records.description: The Equinox EV underdelivers on DC fast charging relative to rivals: independent tests show peak power drops sharply (thermal derate) after roughly 10 minutes, falling from ~154 kW to as low as ~63 kW by ~29% SOC, with 10-80% sessions taking ~50 minutes on both 150 kW and 350 kW stations. The cause is the pack's low ~288 V nominal architecture (requiring very high amperage to hit peak) plus conservative battery thermal management on this first-generation Ultium platform. Owners also report occasional charging stalls/handshake failures at public stations.
records.solution: Pre-condition the battery before fast charging when possible, use high-current stations, and keep the vehicle on the latest software (GM has tuned charging behavior via updates). Persistent stalls at one station should be reported and rechecked against another charger to isolate vehicle- vs. charger-side faults. This is a platform characteristic, not a recall.
symptoms: DC fast-charge rate well below the rated peak
Charge speed drops sharply after about 10 minutes (thermal derate)
Minimal benefit from 350 kW vs 150 kW stations
Charging session stalls or fails to initiate at public chargers
Longer-than-expected 10-80% charge times (~50 min)

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain and Charging System Issues
records.description: The 2024 Equinox EV experiences 12V auxiliary battery drain issues, with ancillary systems drawing power from the 12V battery nearly constantly even when the vehicle is off. GM released software update N25-249834 to improve 12V battery charging behavior and reduce drain. If the HV battery falls below 12% state of charge, the automatic 12V maintenance mode stops working, leaving the 12V battery to drain completely. Dead 12V battery prevents the vehicle from starting even with a full HV battery.
records.solution: Visit dealer for software update N25-249834 which improves 12V battery management. Keep the vehicle plugged in when parked for extended periods to maintain both HV and 12V batteries. If the 12V battery dies, use the jump-start terminals under the front hood. Consider a trickle charger for vehicles stored for more than a week.
symptoms: Vehicle fails to start after sitting for several days
12V battery warning messages on display
SHVS (Stop/Start) system warning messages
Electronics behave erratically at startup
Key fob range reduced or fob stops communicating

citations.title: 12V Battery Failure Reports - Equinox EV Forum

communityRecommendations.content: Always keep the Equinox EV plugged in when parked for more than 2-3 days. The 12V battery maintenance mode only works when the HV battery is above 12% charge. If you let the HV battery get too low, the 12V battery will also die. Ask the dealer about software update N25-249834

The 12V AGM battery is located under the front hood and can be jump-started using standard terminals. Keep a portable jump starter in the vehicle as a precaution until the software update is confirmed installed on your vehicle

records.title: Adaptive Cruise Control Braking Failure
records.description: The 2025 Equinox EV (and some late-production 2024 models) were recalled for an adaptive cruise control issue where the system may fail to apply the brakes when approaching a slower vehicle or stopped traffic. The issue is related to software calibration in the forward collision avoidance system. This creates a serious collision risk when the driver relies on adaptive cruise control for following distance management.
records.solution: Contact Chevrolet dealer for a software update to the adaptive cruise control and forward collision avoidance system. Do not rely solely on adaptive cruise control for collision avoidance. Always be prepared to brake manually. The fix is a free software update under the recall.
symptoms: Adaptive cruise control does not slow down for vehicles ahead
Forward collision warning does not trigger when expected
Vehicle maintains speed when approaching stopped traffic
Adaptive cruise control disengages without warning
Inconsistent braking response in ACC mode

citations.title: 2025 Chevy Equinox EV Recalled for Cruise-Control Braking Issue

records.title: Regenerative Braking Inconsistency and One-Pedal Driving Jerkiness
records.description: The regenerative braking system exhibits inconsistent behavior depending on battery state of charge and temperature. One-pedal driving mode can feel jerky or abrupt at low speeds, and the transition between regenerative and friction braking is not always smooth. Cold weather significantly reduces regen capacity.
records.solution: GM has released software updates that improve regen braking calibration — ensure the latest version is installed. Pre-condition the battery in cold weather by using the scheduled departure feature. If the jerkiness is severe, the dealer can recalibrate the brake blending module. Regen limitations in cold weather are normal for all EVs.
symptoms: Jerky deceleration in one-pedal mode
Inconsistent braking feel
Regen reduced warning in cold weather
Abrupt transition from regen to friction braking

records.title: Pedestrian Alert Sound System Non-Compliance Recall
records.description: GM recalled 23,700 model year 2024 Equinox EV vehicles due to an incorrect software calibration in the pedestrian alert sound system. The vehicles do not produce a sufficient change in volume when accelerating from a stopped position to 10 km/h (6.2 mph), failing to meet FMVSS 141 Section 5.4 requirements. This means pedestrians and cyclists may not hear the approaching vehicle at low speeds, increasing the risk of pedestrian-vehicle incidents.
records.solution: Contact Chevrolet dealer for recall service. The fix requires a body control module (BCM) software update. The 2025 model year uses a different noise generation strategy that will likely be adapted for 2024 models. Contact Chevrolet at 1-800-222-1020 with recall number N252527170.
symptoms: Vehicle is unusually quiet when accelerating from a stop
Pedestrians not reacting to vehicle approach at low speeds
No change in exterior warning sound volume from 0-6 mph
Recall notification letter received
Pedestrian alert sound noticeably quieter than other EVs

records.title: Infotainment and Vehicle Software Glitches Requiring Reboot
records.description: As a first-model-year EV on GM's Ultium platform, the Equinox EV experiences various software glitches including infotainment freezing, incorrect range estimates, phantom driver assistance warnings, and occasional 12V auxiliary battery management issues. These are typical new-platform teething problems.
records.solution: Keep the vehicle software updated via OTA updates — GM is actively pushing fixes. Perform a vehicle reset by parking, locking, and waiting 5 minutes before restarting. For persistent issues, the dealer can perform a full system reflash. The 12V battery may need replacement if it was drained by a software bug.
symptoms: Infotainment screen freezes or goes black
Incorrect range estimate
False collision warnings
Vehicle fails to enter Ready mode
12V battery drain overnight
